item.title: Minister to raise Longford concerns with Garda Commissioner
item.description: The Minister for Justice is to raise the ever-increasing violence in Longford town with the Garda Commissioner. On Monday, two men, one in his 20s and the other in his 30s suffered serious injuries in a double stabbing in the county town. While it emerged at this week's meeting of Longford County Council that of the nine officers that have left Longford since December, only two have been replaced. item.title: Yellow snow and ice warning issued to local region
item.description: The Shannonside region has been issued with a status yellow rain and snow warning. It's in effect in Longford, Leitrim, Roscommon, Cavan and Donegal from midnight tonight for 24 hours, while Cork and Kerry face a yellow alert for rain. The entire country will be under a Status Yellow low temperature and ice warning from 9pm tonight until 10am tomorrow morning. item.title: Longford housing sees unprecedented demand
item.description: There has been an overwhelming response to a new affordable housing scheme in Longford. A total of 150 expressions of interest have been received for 25 affordable homes at Ard Michael, located on the Ballinalee Road. The homes, which are part of a local authority-led affordable purchase scheme, are aimed at helping first-time buyers and eligible applicants get onto the property ladder. item.title: Meeting to discuss the future of Leitrim Community Games
item.description: A meeting has been called amid concerns about the future of Leitrim Community Games. Organisers warn that a lack of volunteers could threaten upcoming competitions within the county. The roles of joint chairperson, treasurer, PRO are yet to be filled. Advertisement Without new volunteers stepping forward, organisers say it will be increasingly difficult to manage registrations, communications, finances, and the delivery of local and county-level activities. item.title: Landowners urged to cut overgrown hedges
item.description: The Road Safety Authority says overgrown hedges and tree branches need to be cut back by the end of the month. The RSA and the County and City Management Association are reminding farmers and landowners of their responsibilities to trim and maintain hedgerows by the end of February. Hedge-cutting is banned between the 1st of March and 31st of August to allow birds and wildlife to nest and take shelter. item.title: Ireland's first ESA Phi-Lab to be based in Mullingar
item.description: A new first-of-its-kind space innovation centre in Mullingar is expected to put Ireland at the forefront of European space research. Phi-Lab will support space technology, AI and advanced manufacturing. It’s backed by a Government investment of 170 million euro over the next five years. item.title: Overcrowding continues at local hospitals
item.description: There were almost 60 admitted patients waiting for a bed at local hospitals this morning. That's according to the INMO's latest trolley watch report. Friday's figures show there were 44 patients waiting in Sligo University Hospital. Advertisement This included 25 in the emergency department and 19 on wards elsewhere. While there were 13 patients waiting in Portiuncula.

item.title: Longford man jailed for one year for harassing local solicitor
item.description: A Longford man has been jailed for one year for harassing a local solicitor, including falsely accusing her of killing children. The solicitor has outlined the devastating impact it had on her. At Longford Circuit Court on Tuesday, 54-year-old Patrick Cassidy, of Dromard, Moyne, pleaded guilty to harassing Longford solicitor Pauline Brady between January 1, 2024, and January 7, 2025. item.title: Man accused of New Year's Day assault in Ballagh further remanded on bail
item.description: A man accused of a serious assault in Ballaghaderreen, which led to the death of another man, has been further remanded on bail. Englishman Jorden Newin suffered serious injuries after the alleged assault in the early hours of New Year’s Day. The 39-year-old later died in hospital. Advertisement Yevhen Shutko, 46, who lives in Co Roscommon, was charged with assault causing serious harm last month. He re-appeared in Ballaghaderreen District Court today and was remanded on bail until March 13th.

item.title: Over 360 patients waiting over 18 months for treatment at local hospitals
item.description: Over 360 patients are waiting over 18 months for treatment at local hospitals. The most recent report from the National Treatment Purchase Fund reveals just over 5,300 inpatients were on the waiting list as of the end of January. A total of 5,330 are languishing on outpatient waiting lists at Sligo, Roscommon, Portiuncula and Mullingar hospitals. Advertisement As of the 31st of January, this number included 189 children.
